policy_title: Reduce Health Inequalities and Prioritise Women's Health
stated: Labour will tackle the social determinants of health, aiming to halve the gap in healthy life expectancy between the richest and poorest regions in England. They will prioritise women’s health during NHS reform and commission a new HIV action plan to eradicate new cases by 2030.

source.quote: As part of our health mission, Labour will tackle the social determinants of health, halving the gap in healthy life expectancy between the richest and poorest regions in England. Labour will prioritise women’s health as we reform the NHS. Labour will commission a new HIV action plan in England, in pursuit of ending HIV cases by 2030.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS reform (women's health prioritisation, HIV action plan) and health outcomes (halving the healthy-life-expectancy gap between regions), all of which bear materially on healthcare access and capacity.
The explicit, named goal is to halve the healthy life expectancy gap between the richest and poorest regions of England — this is a direct regional inequality indicator squarely within O14's scope.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O3 for the direct NHS/health-service interventions, O14 for the explicit targeting of the rich-poor regional health gap. Social determinants work flows through these two fundamentals rather than warranting additional bearings — its effect on O2, O13 or O15 would be incidental and not mechanistically pinned to specific indicators by the policy text.
